The test `test_min_max_ordered_empty` checks whether the `min` function on a categorical array with an empty list of categories works as expected. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case.

Following the execution path, we find that when creating a Categorical object, the `_codes` attribute is initialized in two different ways depending on the `fastpath` parameter.

In one case (when `fastpath=True`), the `_codes` attribute is set to the result of `coerce_indexer_dtype(values, dtype.categories)`. However, in this specific test case (`test_min_max_ordered_empty`), the `categories` list is empty. 

Looking at the code snippet for `Categorical.__init__`, we see that when `dtype.categories` is None (which it is in this case), no special action is taken to set `_codes`.

Therefore, when calling `cat.min()`, the `_codes` attribute of the Categorical object is not properly initialized, leading to a ValueError when trying to find the minimum code.

Consequently, the error demonstrated by the test is due to the fact that the `_codes` attribute of the categorical array is not correctly set up for empty categories.
